properties.name: The default log filter is quiet for dependencies and loud for reflow2 — an uncapped container log can fill a host disk
properties.rationale:
FOUND BY A USER'S QUESTION RATHER THAN BY ANY CHECK. Anthony's laptop had been filled by a docker container log — not reflow2's — and asking whether reflow2 used a particular cache path led to measuring what reflow2's own container would do in the same situation. The answer was that it ships the same hazard: no RUST_LOG default, no logging guidance in the image, and a filter that lets a dependency dominate the stream.

The reflow2-specific lesson is that we publish a container and had never asked what its log does over time. A design that models deployment environments had nothing recorded about the one operational property most likely to take a host down.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: how large a real reflow2 container log actually grows per unit of work. The 78% figure is a ratio measured on a development server over 473 lines, not a rate measured on a deployed one. The fix is right regardless — an operator does not want a dependency's commit bookkeeping at info — but nobody has measured the absolute number.
properties.summary:
MEASURED ON THIS PROJECT'S OWN SERVER LOG, 2026-09-08: 368 of 473 lines — 78% — were `tantivy`'s per-commit and garbage-collect bookkeeping, against 11 lines from reflow2 itself. The default filter was a bare `info`, which lets every dependency's info-level chatter through.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. In a container that stream is stderr, and Docker's default `json-file` driver has NO SIZE LIMIT, so a long-running reflow2 server grows an unbounded log almost entirely out of a dependency's internal bookkeeping. That failure presents as the whole HOST dying rather than as anything wrong with the container, which is the worst shape a failure can take.

THE FIX: the default becomes `warn,reflow2_mcp=info,reflow2_core=info`. Stated as "quiet everything, then raise our own" rather than as `tantivy=warn`, deliberately — silencing the one dependency that happens to be noisy today leaves the next one to be discovered the same way. RUST_LOG still overrides all of it.

MEASURED END TO END on one import: 15 lines to 6, all nine tantivy lines gone, and the ERROR still comes through in full — the check that matters, since a quieter log that hides failures would be a worse defect than the one being fixed. `RUST_LOG=info` restores all 15.

PINNED AS A SHAPE, NOT A LITERAL: the filter is a named const and the test asserts the global default is quiet, that both reflow2 crates are raised above it, and that the string parses as an EnvFilter. Asserting the exact string would make any future addition a test edit rather than a decision. OBSERVED TO FAIL by negative control — restoring the bare `info` this replaced fails it on exactly the global-default assertion.

The Dockerfile now tells an operator to run with `--log-opt max-size`, because reflow2 can only reduce the RATE; only the driver's cap bounds the TOTAL.
